question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.
Just bite the ______ and tell him the truth.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. bullet.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "Bite the bullet" means to face a difficult, unpleasant, or painful situation with courage and resolve, especially after a period of hesitation. (साहस के साथ कठिन परिस्थिति का सामना करना)
◦ Example: Just bite the bullet and tell him the truth.

• The expression is said to originate from the practice of having a wounded soldier bite on a bullet to cope with the pain during surgery, before anaesthesia was common.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "gun" does not form part of any standard idiom that fits this context; "bite the gun" is not an English idiom.

• Option 3: "dust" — the idiom "bite the dust" means to die or to fail/be defeated, which does not fit the meaning of facing the truth courageously.

• Option 4: "shot" does not form any recognised idiom with "bite"; it is a distractor based on its association with "bullet" and "gun".

NOTE

• Other idioms with "bite": "Bite the dust" (to fail or die), "Bite off more than one can chew" (to take on more than one can handle), and "Once bitten, twice shy" (cautious after a bad experience).

• Do not confuse "bite the bullet" with "bite the dust" — both involve hardship, but only the former means facing something difficult head-on.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.
I like bread made up of corn ___________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. flour.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence talks about "bread made up of corn ___________", which requires the word "flour" — the fine powder made by grinding grain (here, corn/maize) that is used to make bread, cakes, etc.

• "Flour" and "flower" are homophones (words that sound alike but have different meanings and spellings) — "flour" is the powdered grain used in baking, while "flower" is the reproductive part of a plant.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "flower" is incorrect — it refers to the blossom of a plant, not a baking ingredient, and is only a homophone trap for "flour".

• Option 3: "floor" is incorrect — it means the base/ground surface of a room, unrelated to bread-making.

• Option 4: "failure" is incorrect — it means lack of success, and makes no sense in the context of bread.

NOTE

• Other common homophone pairs tested in SSC exams: hear/here, there/their/they're, quiet/quite, principal/principle, stationary/stationery, and dessert/desert.

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.
Loud enough to be heard.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Audible.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Audible" means loud enough or clear enough to be heard. (सुनने योग्य / सुनाई देने वाला)
◦ Example: Please speak louder; your voice is barely audible from the back of the hall.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "Audit" (लेखा परीक्षा): an official inspection of an organisation's financial accounts.

• Option 3: "Audacious" (साहसी/ढीठ): showing a willingness to take bold risks; recklessly bold.

• Option 4: "Audacity" (धृष्टता): the quality of being bold or impudent, often disrespectfully so.

NOTE

• All four options share the Latin root "audire" (to hear) or "audax" (bold), which is a common source of confusion; remember "audible" relates to hearing/sound, while "audacious/audacity" relate to boldness.

• Other one-word substitutes with "-ible/-able": Legible (able to be read), Visible (able to be seen), Edible (fit to be eaten).

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.
Insert
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Remove.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Insert" means to put or fit something into something else. (डालना / सम्मिलित करना) Its opposite is "Remove", meaning to take something out or away from a place. (हटाना)
◦ Example: She had to remove the old battery before she could insert the new one.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "Inform" (सूचित करना): to give someone facts or information; not an antonym of "insert".

• Option 3: "Select" (चुनना): to choose from a range of options; unrelated in meaning to "insert".

• Option 4: "Inject" (इंजेक्ट करना): to force a liquid into something, which is actually close in meaning to "insert" (a near-synonym), not its opposite.

NOTE

• Be careful with "Inject", which is a common distractor here precisely because it resembles "insert" in meaning rather than being its opposite.

• Other antonym pairs of this type: Include × Exclude, Attach × Detach, Add × Subtract.

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined word in the given sentence.
Verity is a good virtue for human life.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Truth.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Verity" means a true principle or belief, especially one of fundamental importance; truth. (सत्य / सच्चाई)
◦ Example: He spoke of eternal verities such as honesty and justice.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Knowledge" (ज्ञान): facts, information and skills acquired through experience or education — broader than "verity" and not a direct synonym.

• Option 3: "Information" (जानकारी): facts provided or learned about something; again broader and not specific to truthfulness.

• Option 4: "Cooperation" (सहयोग): the process of working together towards a common end; unrelated in meaning to "verity".

NOTE

• "Verity" is related to the word "verify" (to confirm the truth of) and "veracity" (truthfulness, accuracy) — all share the Latin root "verus" meaning "true".

• Do not confuse "verity" with "vanity" (excessive pride) — they look similar but are unrelated in meaning.

question:
Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful sentence.
Founding father / is / of / New Historicism / Greenbalt / considered / the.
option_1: The founding father of New Historicism is considered Greenbalt.
option_2: The founding father is considered Greenbalt of New Historicism.
option_3: Greenbalt is considered the founding father of New Historicism.
option_4: Greenbelt is the founding father of New Historicism considered.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Greenbalt is considered the founding father of New Historicism.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• To arrange jumbled parts into a meaningful sentence, first identify the subject, verb and object/complement, then arrange them in the standard Subject + Verb + Complement order.

• Here, the subject is "Greenbalt", the verb phrase is "is considered", and the complement is "the founding father of New Historicism", giving: Greenbalt is considered the founding father of New Historicism.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "The founding father of New Historicism is considered Greenbalt." is grammatically inverted and awkward — it wrongly makes "the founding father" the subject and "Greenbalt" the complement, reversing the natural sense.

• Option 2: "The founding father is considered Greenbalt of New Historicism." incorrectly attaches "of New Historicism" to "Greenbalt" instead of to "the founding father", distorting the meaning.

• Option 4: "Greenbelt is the founding father of New Historicism considered." places the verb "considered" wrongly at the end of the sentence, making it grammatically incorrect.

NOTE

• In parts-rearrangement questions, always locate the main subject and verb first, then fit the remaining phrases around them so that the sentence reads naturally and logically.

• (As a point of general knowledge, the American literary critic Stephen Greenblatt is widely regarded as the founder of the school of literary theory known as New Historicism.)

question:
Select the option that expresses the following sentence in active voice.
The issue has been successfully resolved by the customer care team.
option_1: The customer care team successfully resolves the issue.
option_2: The customer care team successfully resolved the issue.
option_3: The issue has successfully resolved the customer care team.
option_4: The customer care team has successfully resolved the issue.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. The customer care team has successfully resolved the issue.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The given sentence "The issue has been successfully resolved by the customer care team" is in the Present Perfect Tense, Passive Voice.

• Rule — Present Perfect Tense:
◦ Passive: Object + has/have + been + V3 + by + Subject
◦ Active: Subject + has/have + V3 + Object

• Applying the rule: the agent "the customer care team" (after "by") becomes the subject; the auxiliary "has been" becomes simply "has"; the past participle "resolved" is retained; and the original subject "the issue" becomes the object.
◦ Active: The customer care team has successfully resolved the issue.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 is incorrect because "resolves" (Simple Present) does not match the Present Perfect tense of the original sentence.

• Option 2 is incorrect because "resolved" alone (without "has") represents the Simple Past Tense, not the Present Perfect Tense.

• Option 3 is incorrect because the subject and object have been interchanged wrongly, producing the illogical meaning that the issue has resolved the customer care team.

NOTE

• When converting Passive to Active voice, the tense of the sentence must always be preserved exactly — only the subject and object switch places and the auxiliary changes form.

• Present Perfect Passive is easily identified by the structure "has/have been + V3".

question:
Select the most appropriate verb / verb phrase to fill in the blank.
The team ________________ the championship before their star player got injured.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. had won.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence describes two past actions, one of which happened before the other. The later action, "got injured", is in the Simple Past Tense.

• Rule — Past Perfect Tense: When two actions occur in the past, the action that happened first (earlier) is expressed in the Past Perfect Tense (had + V3), and the action that happened later is expressed in the Simple Past Tense (V2). The word "before" signals which action came first.

• Here, winning the championship happened before the player got injured, so the earlier action "win" must take the Past Perfect form: "had won".
◦ The team had won the championship before their star player got injured.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "was won" is incorrect because it is a passive construction, which does not fit the active sense required, and it does not indicate the earlier of two past events.

• Option 3: "has won" is incorrect because the Present Perfect Tense is not used for an action completed before another past action.

• Option 4: "win" is incorrect because the base form is not marked for any past time reference at all.

NOTE

• Clue words like "before", "after", "already", "by the time" in a sentence with two past events are strong indicators that the Past Perfect Tense is required for the earlier action.

• Compare: "The train had left before I reached the station" — same pattern of Past Perfect + Simple Past.

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.
Money collected from people for a cause.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Fund.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "Fund" means a sum of money saved or collected for a particular purpose or cause. (किसी उद्देश्य के लिए एकत्रित धनराशि)
◦ Example: The school set up a relief fund to help flood victims.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Collection" (संग्रह): a general term for a group of things gathered together, not specifically money gathered for a cause.

• Option 2: "Deposit" (जमा राशि): a sum of money placed in a bank or given as part payment/security, not necessarily collected from people for a cause.

• Option 4: "Savings" (बचत): money that a person keeps aside from their own income, not money collected from other people.

NOTE

• Related one-word substitutions: "Donation" — something given, especially money, to a cause; "Philanthropist" — a person who donates generously to good causes; "Charity" — voluntary giving of help to those in need.

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can rectify the incorrectly spelt word in the following sentence.
In our quest for power, we often fail to acknowlege the existence of other people.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. acknowledge.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct spelling is "acknowledge" — meaning to accept or admit the existence or truth of something.

• Spelling key: ACKNOWLEDGE = A + C + K + N + O + W + L + E + D + G + E. Note the silent "d" before "ge" at the end — a commonly dropped letter — and only a single "c".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "acknowledje" is incorrect — the ending "-dje" is wrong; it should be "-dge".

• Option 2: "accknowledge" is incorrect — there is an extra, incorrect double "c"; the word has only one "c".

• Option 4: "acknowlede" is incorrect — the letter "g" has been dropped from the correct ending "-dge".

NOTE

• Other words that commonly drop the silent "d" or "g" in student spelling errors: "judgement/judgment", "pledge", "knowledge", "bridge".

• "Acknowledge" is related to "knowledge" — both share the root idea of "knowing"; the related noun form is "acknowledgement".

question:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.
A. He remembered her as she once was – an eager, glowing girl.
B. He had not seen her for nearly thirteen years.
C. Mr. Satterthwaite went to meet her.
D. And now he saw – a Frozen Lady.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. CBAD.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In paragraph-rearrangement questions, identify the sentence that logically introduces the topic/action, then trace the sequence of events or ideas that follow from it.

• Sentence C ("Mr. Satterthwaite went to meet her") is the natural opener — it introduces the subject (Mr. Satterthwaite) and the action (going to meet "her").

• Sentence B ("He had not seen her for nearly thirteen years") logically follows, explaining the background — why the meeting is significant, since it had been a long gap.

• Sentence A ("He remembered her as she once was — an eager, glowing girl") follows next, describing his memory of her from the past.

• Sentence D ("And now he saw — a Frozen Lady") comes last, contrasting his old memory with what he actually sees now, giving the paragraph a logical and dramatic conclusion.
◦ Correct order: C → B → A → D.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "DCBA" is incorrect because it begins with the concluding, climactic sentence D, which makes no sense without the preceding context.

• Option 3: "DBAC" is incorrect for the same reason — it opens with the climax (D) before the reader knows who is being discussed.

• Option 4: "ABCD" is incorrect because it starts with his memory of her (A) before establishing that he went to meet her at all (C), breaking the logical sequence.

NOTE

• In such questions, look for pronouns ("he", "her") — a sentence that introduces a proper noun subject (like "Mr. Satterthwaite") usually comes before sentences that merely refer to "he"/"her".

• Also look for words like "now" (in D) which typically signal a contrast with something described earlier, and therefore belong later in the sequence.

question:
Identify from the given options the word which is similar in meaning to the following word.
Munificent
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Magnanimous.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Munificent" means extremely generous or lavish in giving. (अत्यंत उदार)
◦ Example: The billionaire made a munificent donation to the hospital.

• "Magnanimous" means generous or forgiving, especially towards a rival or a less powerful person, and is used here as the closest match in meaning to "munificent" (generosity of spirit/giving).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "Malicious" (द्वेषपूर्ण): having or showing a desire to harm someone; the opposite spirit of "munificent".

• Option 3: "Miserly" (कंजूस): extremely unwilling to spend money; a direct antonym of "munificent", not a synonym.

• Option 4: "Underappreciated" (कम सराहा गया): not valued or recognised as much as deserved; unrelated in meaning to generosity.

NOTE

• Other synonyms of "munificent"/generous: "Bountiful", "Benevolent", "Philanthropic", "Lavish".

• Do not confuse "munificent" (generous) with "magnificent" (splendid, grand) — they look alike but differ in meaning, though "magnanimous" here correctly captures the generosity sense.

question:
Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful sentence.
P) once said
Q) a wise man
R) that action speaks
S) louder than words
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. QPRS.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• To rearrange jumbled parts, first identify the subject of the sentence, then the verb, then the reported clause that follows.

• The subject is "a wise man" (Q), followed by the verb phrase "once said" (P), followed by the reported clause "that action speaks" (R), completed by "louder than words" (S).
◦ Correct order: Q → P → R → S, giving: "A wise man once said that action speaks louder than words."

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "QSRP" is incorrect because it places "louder than words" (S) immediately after the subject, breaking the sense before the verb "said" even appears.

• Option 3: "PQRS" is incorrect because it begins with "once said" before naming the subject "a wise man", making it grammatically backwards.

• Option 4: "SQPR" is incorrect because it begins with the concluding phrase "louder than words", which cannot logically start the sentence.

NOTE

• "Action speaks louder than words" is itself a well-known proverb meaning that what a person actually does matters more than what they say.

• In reported-speech-style sentence formation, the pattern Subject + said/says + that + clause is a common structure to look for in jumbled-parts questions.

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom.
Bincy's mother kept her cards close to her chest.
option_2: Informed that all the cards must be kept safe
option_3: Kept her purse and money by herself
option_4: Kept her plans and thoughts hidden
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Kept her plans and thoughts hidden.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "to keep one's cards close to one's chest" means to be secretive about one's plans, intentions, or thoughts, and not reveal them to others. (अपनी योजनाओं को गुप्त रखना)
◦ Example: The manager kept her cards close to her chest about the upcoming layoffs.

• The idiom comes from card games, where a player holds their cards close to their body so that opponents cannot see them and guess their strategy.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Decided to show more affection" is incorrect — the idiom has nothing to do with affection.

• Option 2: "Informed that all the cards must be kept safe" is incorrect — this is a literal misreading of "cards" rather than the idiomatic meaning.

• Option 3: "Kept her purse and money by herself" is incorrect — this is also a literal (non-idiomatic) misinterpretation.

NOTE

• Other idioms related to secrecy: "To play one's cards right" (to act cleverly to gain advantage), "To be tight-lipped" (to say very little), and "To keep something under wraps" (to keep something secret).

question:
Identify the error in the given sentence.
My colleague always works latest than me.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. latest.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence uses the comparative structure "than", which requires a word in the comparative degree, not the superlative degree.

• Rule: The superlative degree (e.g., "latest", "best", "fastest") is used to compare three or more things and is never followed by "than". The comparative degree (e.g., "later", "better", "faster") is used to compare two things and is followed by "than".

• Here, only two people are being compared — "my colleague" and "me" — so the comparative form "later" must be used instead of the superlative "latest".
◦ Correct sentence: "My colleague always works later than me."

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "My colleague" is grammatically correct as the subject of the sentence.

• Option 3: "always works" is grammatically correct — a Simple Present Tense verb agreeing with the singular subject "My colleague".

• Option 4: "than me." is grammatically correct as the comparative complement, once the comparative adjective "later" is used earlier in the sentence.

NOTE

• Never use a superlative degree adjective/adverb with "than" — this is one of the most frequently tested error-spotting rules in SSC exams.

• Similarly, "most" (superlative) should not be followed by "than"; only "more" (comparative) is followed by "than".

question:
Select the option that expresses the following sentence in passive voice.
Gill scored 3 centuries in Tata IPL 2023
option_1: 3 centuries has been scored by Gill in Tata IPL 2023.
option_2: 3 centuries were scored by Gill in Tata IPL 2023.
option_3: 3 centuries had been scored by Gill in Tata IPL 2023.
option_4: 3 centuries were being scored by Gill in Tata IPL 2023.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. 3 centuries were scored by Gill in Tata IPL 2023.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence "Gill scored 3 centuries in Tata IPL 2023" is in the Simple Past Tense, Active Voice.

• Rule — Simple Past Tense:
◦ Active: Subject + V2 + Object
◦ Passive: Object + was/were + V3 + by + Subject

• Applying the rule: the object "3 centuries" (plural) becomes the subject, so the auxiliary is "were"; the verb "scored" becomes the past participle "scored" (same form here); and "Gill" becomes the agent with "by".
◦ Passive: 3 centuries were scored by Gill in Tata IPL 2023.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 is incorrect because "has been scored" is Present Perfect passive, which does not match the Simple Past tense of the original sentence.

• Option 3 is incorrect because "had been scored" is Past Perfect passive, used only when this action happened before another past action, which is not indicated here.

• Option 4 is incorrect because "were being scored" is Past Continuous passive, suggesting an action that was ongoing, whereas scoring 3 centuries is a completed action.

NOTE

• Always match the passive voice tense exactly to the tense of the original active sentence — only the subject/object positions and auxiliary form change.

• With plural objects becoming the subject (like "3 centuries"), the auxiliary must also be plural: "were", not "was".

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.
Carcass
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Corpse.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Carcass" means the dead body of an animal (or, informally, a person). (शव / मृत शरीर, विशेषतः पशु का)
◦ Example: Vultures were circling above the carcass of the deer.

• "Corpse" means a dead body, most commonly used for a human but broadly synonymous with "carcass" in the sense of a dead body.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Gale" (तेज़ आंधी): a very strong wind; unrelated in meaning.

• Option 2: "Scrap" (टुकड़ा / कबाड़): a small leftover piece, or discarded/waste material; unrelated to a dead body.

• Option 3: "Prison" (कारागार): a place where criminals are kept in confinement; unrelated in meaning.

NOTE

• Related words: "Cadaver" (a dead body, especially one used for medical study) and "Carrion" (the decaying flesh of dead animals) are close synonyms of "carcass".

question: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Atrocios.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "Atrocios" is spelt incorrectly; the correct spelling is "Atrocious" — meaning extremely wicked, cruel, or (informally) very bad/unpleasant.

• Spelling key: ATROCIOUS = A + T + R + O + C + I + O + U + S. Note the "-ious" ending (not "-ios"), which is a common ending for adjectives derived from Latin, such as "gracious", "precious", "vicious".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Accessibility" is spelt correctly — the quality of being able to be reached, entered, or used.

• Option 2: "Aptitude" is spelt correctly — a natural ability to do something.

• Option 3: "Apparatus" is spelt correctly — equipment or a set of materials needed for a particular purpose.

NOTE

• Words ending in "-ious": gracious, precious, vicious, spacious, atrocious, ambitious — remember the full "-ious" ending, not a shortened "-ios".

• Always double-check adjective endings like "-ious", "-eous", and "-uous", which are commonly mis-spelt in SSC exams.

question:
Select the correct ANTONYM of the underlined word to fill in the blank and complete the following sentence.
He is always active in a party but _______ in the class.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. inert.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Active" means engaging or ready to engage in physically energetic pursuits; lively and dynamic. (सक्रिय) Its antonym is "inert", meaning lacking the ability or strength to move; sluggish, inactive. (निष्क्रिय)
◦ Example: He is always active in a party but inert in the class.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "careless" (लापरवाह): not giving sufficient attention; not the direct opposite of "active".

• Option 3: "angry" (क्रोधित): feeling or showing strong annoyance; unrelated in meaning to "active".

• Option 4: "naughty" (शरारती): badly behaved, mischievous; not an antonym of "active".

NOTE

• Other synonyms of "inert": "lethargic", "passive", "dormant", "sluggish" — all commonly tested as antonyms of "active"/"energetic" in SSC exams.

• "Inert" is also a chemistry term (an inert gas does not readily react), which can help in remembering its sense of "not active".

question:
Select the option that expresses the opposite meaning of the underlined word.
In front of the big screen, this behaviour is generally considered taboo.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Acceptable.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Taboo" means a social or cultural custom prohibiting or restricting a particular practice or association with a particular thing or person; forbidden or disapproved of. (वर्जित / निषिद्ध) Its opposite is "Acceptable", meaning able to be tolerated or allowed; permitted by social convention. (स्वीकार्य)
◦ Example: In front of the big screen, this behaviour is generally considered acceptable.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Obedience" (आज्ञाकारिता): the quality of complying with a command or law; not an antonym of "taboo".

• Option 3: "Promotion" (पदोन्नति): advancement in rank or position, or the act of encouraging something; unrelated in meaning.

• Option 4: "Prescription" (नुस्खा): an instruction, especially a medical one, or a formal recommendation; unrelated in meaning.

NOTE

• Other synonyms of "taboo": "forbidden", "prohibited", "proscribed"; other antonyms: "permitted", "allowed", "sanctioned".

question:
Comprehension:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Social media companies (1)______ claim that they promote democracy and are dedicated to the empowerment of ordinary individuals. The assertion (2)______ entirely unfounded. Recent history shows how (3)______ citizens have been mobilised against totalitarian regimes on social networking sites. Starting from MeToo to Black Lives Matter, digital networks (4)______ indispensable in bringing together critical voices against social and political (5)______ .

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. frequently.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Blank (1) needs a word that describes how often social media companies make this claim about promoting democracy. "Frequently" means often, repeatedly and fits the context of a claim that is commonly and repeatedly made by such companies.
◦ Complete sentence: "Social media companies frequently claim that they promote democracy and are dedicated to the empowerment of ordinary individuals."

• The rest of the passage goes on to examine and qualify this claim, which only makes sense if the claim is one that is made often/routinely, not rarely or never.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "seldom" means rarely, which would suggest the claim is uncommon — this contradicts the passage's later discussion, which treats the claim as a well-known, often-repeated assertion.

• Option 3: "never" would mean the companies do not make this claim at all, which contradicts the sentence structure that goes on to state and then examine the claim.

• Option 4: "don't" is grammatically and logically incorrect here, as it would negate the claim entirely, making the rest of the passage (which discusses and questions the claim) meaningless.

NOTE

• In cloze passages, always read the following sentences for contextual clues — here, the passage goes on to discuss whether this claim is "unfounded", which only makes sense if the claim is actually and often made.

• Frequency adverbs commonly tested: always, usually, often, frequently, occasionally, seldom, rarely, never — know their relative strength/frequency.

Comprehension:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Social media companies (1)______ claim that they promote democracy and are dedicated to the empowerment of ordinary individuals. The assertion (2)______ entirely unfounded. Recent history shows how (3)______ citizens have been mobilised against totalitarian regimes on social networking sites. Starting from MeToo to Black Lives Matter, digital networks (4)______ indispensable in bringing together critical voices against social and political (5)______ .

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. may not be.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Blank (2) requires a modal verb phrase that includes the verb "be", since the sentence continues with the adjective phrase "entirely unfounded" — a modal alone (without "be") cannot grammatically connect to an adjective in this structure.
◦ Complete sentence: "The assertion may not be entirely unfounded."

• "May not be" is a hedging modal expression suggesting possibility/uncertainty — here it suggests that the claim (that social media promotes democracy) is not completely without basis, which fits the passage's subsequent point about citizens being mobilised via social media against totalitarian regimes.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "cannot" is grammatically incomplete here — "cannot entirely unfounded" is not a valid sentence, since "cannot" needs a following verb (e.g., "cannot be").

• Option 2: "should" is grammatically incomplete for the same reason — "should entirely unfounded" is not valid without "be".

• Option 3: "shall" is grammatically incomplete for the same reason — it also requires "be" to connect to the adjective "unfounded".

NOTE

• A modal verb (can, could, may, might, should, shall, will, would, must) needs a base verb to complete its meaning — when followed directly by an adjective (like "unfounded"), the linking verb "be" must be included, e.g., "may not be", "should not be", "cannot be".

• This is a frequently tested grammar trap in cloze passages — always check whether the modal phrase is grammatically complete before choosing it.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. common.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Blank (3) needs a word describing the type of citizens who have been mobilised against totalitarian regimes via social media. "Common" means ordinary; belonging to or shared by two or more people/things; not special or exceptional, and fits well with "ordinary individuals" mentioned earlier in the passage.
◦ Complete sentence: "Recent history shows how common citizens have been mobilised against totalitarian regimes on social networking sites."

• The passage's opening line refers to the "empowerment of ordinary individuals", so the word describing the citizens later in the passage should logically echo this idea of ordinariness — "common citizens" (a phrase often used to mean ordinary members of the public).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "alien" means foreign or unfamiliar/belonging to another place, which does not fit the sense of "ordinary individuals" being empowered within their own society.

• Option 3: "neutral" means not aligned with or supporting any side, which does not describe citizens being actively "mobilised" against a regime — mobilised citizens are, by definition, not neutral.

• Option 4: "foreign" means belonging to or from another country, which does not fit the context of citizens acting within their own totalitarian regimes.

NOTE

• Watch for words in a passage that echo or restate an idea introduced earlier (here, "ordinary individuals" → "common citizens") — this repetition/paraphrase is a common technique used to construct cloze passages.

• Commonly confused words: "common" (ordinary, shared) vs. "alien" (foreign, strange) vs. "neutral" (unbiased, uninvolved).

Recent history shows how (3)______ citizens have been mobilised against totalitarian regimes on social networking sites. Starting from MeToo to Black Lives Matter, digital networks (4)______ indispensable in bringing together critical voices against social and political (5)______ .

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. have been.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Blank (4) requires a verb phrase in the Present Perfect Tense, matching the tense used elsewhere in the passage (e.g., "have been mobilised" in the previous sentence) and the ongoing relevance implied by "Starting from MeToo to Black Lives Matter" — movements that began in the past and continue to be relevant.
◦ Complete sentence: "Starting from MeToo to Black Lives Matter, digital networks have been indispensable in bringing together critical voices against social and political (5)."

• Rule — Present Perfect Tense: used for an action/state that began in the past and continues to have relevance or effect up to the present, formed as have/has + V3. Since "digital networks" is plural, the auxiliary is "have", and "been" (V3 of "be") gives the linking verb needed before the adjective "indispensable".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "can" is grammatically incomplete without a following base verb such as "be" (e.g., "can be indispensable"), and does not convey the sense of an ongoing role since these movements began.

• Option 2: "were" would put the sentence in the Simple Past Tense, incorrectly suggesting that digital networks are no longer indispensable now, which contradicts the passage's overall present-day relevance.

• Option 3: "that" is a relative pronoun/conjunction, not a verb, and cannot grammatically complete the sentence in this position.

NOTE

• When a passage describes something that started in the past ("starting from...") and is still true/relevant, the Present Perfect Tense ("have/has been") is the appropriate choice, not the Simple Past.

• Always check subject-verb agreement in cloze passages: plural subjects like "digital networks" take "have", not "has".

Comprehension:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Social media companies (1)______ claim that they promote democracy and are dedicated to the empowerment of ordinary individuals. The assertion (2)______ entirely unfounded. Recent history shows how (3)______ citizens have been mobilised against totalitarian regimes on social networking sites. Starting from MeToo to Black Lives Matter, digital networks (4)______ indispensable in bringing together critical voices against social and political (5)______ .

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. injustice.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Blank (5) needs a noun that pairs naturally with "social and political" and fits the context of movements like MeToo and Black Lives Matter, both of which arose in opposition to unfair treatment. "Injustice" means lack of fairness or justice; an unjust act, and precisely describes what such movements campaign against.
◦ Complete sentence: "...digital networks have been indispensable in bringing together critical voices against social and political injustice."

• The preposition "against" before the blank signals that the missing word must denote something negative that is being opposed — "injustice" fits this logically, since movements like MeToo and Black Lives Matter unite voices specifically against unfair/unjust treatment.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "election" does not fit — "against social and political election" does not make sense, as an election is a neutral democratic process, not something inherently opposed by such movements.

• Option 2: "democracy" is incorrect because these movements are not opposed to democracy; in fact, the passage frames such mobilisation as supportive of democratic empowerment, not against it.

• Option 4: "justice" is incorrect because it is the opposite of what fits — these movements campaign against the ABSENCE of justice (i.e., against injustice), not against justice itself.

NOTE

• Pay close attention to the preposition before a blank (here, "against") — it determines whether a positive or negative noun is required to make logical sense.

• "Injustice" and "justice" are antonyms formed with the negative prefix "in-"; other examples: "equality/inequality", "security/insecurity", "tolerance/intolerance".
